lastText: File ClosedThe Salient, Sealed TwiceContestedAllied Combined Chiefs, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Stalin was pressed hard on Poland's postwar government at Yalta rather than accepted on ambiguous terms: a harder line taken exactly where the historical conference chose accommodation. The Scheldt was cleared before the autumn's offensives rather than after: Antwerp opened weeks early, and the priority error most postwar assessments rank among the campaign's costliest was simply not made. The Mediterranean Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost anyway. Germany's defeat was never a variable Western Allied command decisions controlled, only its timing, its cost, and the shape of the peace that followed it.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
